key_insight: A shallow variational quantum circuit can be trained analytically to mimic Quantum Phase Estimation measurement outcomes without simulating the full quantum circuit, enabling hardware-friendly molecular energy estimation on NISQ devices.
engineering_relevance: This replaces an exponentially costly QPE simulation step with a classically computed training target, making surrogate-based quantum algorithms more practical for near-term quantum hardware.
method: Compute the QPE target distribution classically using the Dirichlet kernel from FCI energy, ancilla count, and evolution time.
Train a shallow VQC to reproduce the QPE distribution on IBM Quantum hardware.
Compare entangler topologies, circuit depths, and dynamical decoupling under multiple distribution metrics.
evidence_signal: Across four experimental stages on H$_2$, the study evaluated linear vs full entanglers, p=1 to 5 layers, and DD/no-DD settings using Hellinger distance, fidelity error, total variation distance, and Jensen-Shannon divergence, recovering chemical-accuracy energy.
watch_item: Performance is tuned to a specific noise profile and small molecular benchmark, so transfer to deeper circuits, larger molecules, or different hardware may require re-optimization.
paper_title: An Analytically Trained Variational Surrogate for Quantum Phase Estimation on NISQ Hardware
